I've seen various discussions about upvoates and downvoates and it's clear there is no common sense of how to use them. Voat should provide guidance.

Reddiquette says this

Vote. If you think something contributes to conversation, upvote it. If you think it does not contribute to the subreddit it is posted in or is off-topic in a particular community, downvote it.

Just to get the ball rolling here, below is a rough outline of how I vote on things personally. I am curious to how other people handle this.

Things I upvote/upvoat:

  • Comments pertaining to the original topic
  • Replies pertaining to the original comment

Things I downvote/downvoat:

  • Highly visible off-topic comment replies; piggyback comments
  • Obvious spam; obvious trolling
  • Lazy comments; comments that demonstrate said person didn't actually read/view the article posted
  • Duplicate comments, but not always - depending on how short / on-topic they are

Things I don't vote on:

  • Jokes - of any kind, unless in a humor / entertainment verse
  • Negative / rude replies to my comments
  • Things I disagree with - If I feel strongly enough, I'll just reply and maybe learn a thing or two
If they present the things you disagree with in a logical, clear way, upvote them. We gotta have debates that shows both of the sides of an argument.

That seems like a fair approach but I think it breaks down if everything is already highly upvoted and equaly visible. It makes sense to me when the post is at zero though.

Do you, by extension, think the voting system is detrimental to open discussion?
How else can we separate the shit from the gems? An utterly randomized comment section would be terrible.

Sort them into one dynamic shitgem stream where users can adjust the number of shits they see per gem.

Or maybe just remov downvoting altogether and use an upvote only system.
So use the facebook system? Also how can people know what is shit and what is a gem?

People sometimes feel weird up voting something they gut wrenchingly disagree with. I think Voat guidance for voting should make special mention that "an upvoat doesn't mean you agree or endorse a message. It means you think it added value and diversity to the conversation."

usually downvoat if something is in the new feed and clearly a mismatch for a particular subverse, or violates one of the rules posted by said subverse. Kind of like helping the moderators, so to speak.

Also, interestingly, Voat allows you to see how each user votes - up and down. Something to think about.
